grades.description: Near-perfect. Intense floral and fruity notes. Rare and commands top prices at specialty auctions.

grades.name: Grade 3 — Premium Commercial
grades.description: Naturals only at this grade. Still flavorful but less clean. Traded on ECX.

grades.name: Grade 4 — Commercial
grades.description: Standard commercial. Some defects noticeable. Bulk export grade.

grades.name: Grade 5 — Below Standard
grades.description: Low quality. Domestic use or discounted export.

steps.detail: Harvest only fully red (ripe) cherries. Reject green and overripe. Can improve grade by 1–2 levels.
Process cherries within 6–12 hours of picking to avoid fermentation defects.
Float cherries in water — defective, hollow beans float and can be removed cheaply.
For washed: ferment 36–48 hours at altitude. Over-fermentation (sour notes) is the #1 defect cause.
Dry on African raised beds (not ground), turn frequently. Target moisture: 10.5–11.5%.
Store parchment in grain bags at <12% RH. Re-mill within 3 months of harvest for best cup quality.

output.countryDefectNote: In Ethiopia, most defects are black beans (over-fermented), insect-damaged, and withered. Key: selective picking + fermentation control.

steps.detail: Harvest only fully red (ripe) cherries. Reject green and overripe. Can improve grade by 1–2 levels.
Process cherries within 6–12 hours of picking to avoid fermentation defects.
Float cherries in water — defective, hollow beans float and can be removed cheaply.
For washed: ferment 36–48 hours at altitude. Over-fermentation (sour notes) is the #1 defect cause.
Dry on African raised beds (not ground), turn frequently. Target moisture: 10.5–11.5%.
Store parchment in grain bags at <12% RH. Re-mill within 3 months of harvest for best cup quality.

grades.name: PB — Peaberry
grades.description: Single oval bean forming where normally two halves would grow. Concentrated flavor. Prized by specialty roasters.

grades.name: AA
grades.description: Kenya's flagship grade. Bright acidity, complex blackcurrant fruit. Commands highest auction prices.

grades.name: AB
grades.description: Mix of A and B screens. Often matches AA quality. Better value for roasters.

grades.name: C
grades.description: Smaller beans. Standard commercial grade.

grades.name: TT
grades.description: Separated by air density. Lighter beans from premium lots.

grades.name: T
grades.description: Low quality. Mostly domestic consumption.

grades.name: MH/ML — Mbuni
grades.description: Natural (dry) processed. Lowest grade. Heavy body but defects.

grades.name: E — Elephant
grades.description: Two beans fused together. Largest but not necessarily best quality.

targetGrade.name: T

steps.detail: Harvest only fully red (ripe) cherries. Reject green and overripe. Can improve grade by 1–2 levels.
Process cherries within 6–12 hours of picking to avoid fermentation defects.
Float cherries in water — defective, hollow beans float and can be removed cheaply.
For washed: ferment 36–48 hours at altitude. Over-fermentation (sour notes) is the #1 defect cause.
Dry on African raised beds (not ground), turn frequently. Target moisture: 10.5–11.5%.
Store parchment in grain bags at <12% RH. Re-mill within 3 months of harvest for best cup quality.

steps.detail: Harvest only fully red (ripe) cherries. Reject green and overripe. Can improve grade by 1–2 levels.
Process cherries within 6–12 hours of picking to avoid fermentation defects.
Float cherries in water — defective, hollow beans float and can be removed cheaply.

Store parchment in grain bags at <12% RH. Re-mill within 3 months of harvest for best cup quality.

steps.detail: Harvest only fully red (ripe) cherries. Reject green and overripe. Can improve grade by 1–2 levels.
Process cherries within 6–12 hours of picking to avoid fermentation defects.
Float cherries in water — defective, hollow beans float and can be removed cheaply.

Dry on African raised beds (not ground), turn frequently. Target moisture: 10.5–11.5%.
Store parchment in grain bags at <12% RH. Re-mill within 3 months of harvest for best cup quality.

steps.detail: Harvest only fully red (ripe) cherries. Reject green and overripe. Can improve grade by 1–2 levels.
Process cherries within 6–12 hours of picking to avoid fermentation defects.
Float cherries in water — defective, hollow beans float and can be removed cheaply.

Dry on African raised beds (not ground), turn frequently. Target moisture: 10.5–11.5%.
Store parchment in grain bags at <12% RH. Re-mill within 3 months of harvest for best cup quality.

steps.detail: Harvest only fully red (ripe) cherries. Reject green and overripe. Can improve grade by 1–2 levels.
Process cherries within 6–12 hours of picking to avoid fermentation defects.
Float cherries in water — defective, hollow beans float and can be removed cheaply.
For washed: ferment 36–48 hours at altitude. Over-fermentation (sour notes) is the #1 defect cause.
Dry on African raised beds (not ground), turn frequently. Target moisture: 10.5–11.5%.
Store parchment in grain bags at <12% RH. Re-mill within 3 months of harvest for best cup quality.
